first_impression.reaction: Headline's a bit clickbaity ('You Did Not Know?'), so I went straight to the FAQ expecting fluff. The answers cite a village record and the palace, not 'experts say'. Then the intro says 'where a detail comes from the royal palace in Yogyakarta, we say so'. OK, that's the sort of distinction I want, so I kept reading.

journey.quote: Customs vary by family, faith and region, and where a detail comes from the royal palace in Yogyakarta, we say so.
journey.reaction: Good. They're separating court practice from what normal families do, and most culture pages blur those together.

journey.section: What is a traditional Javanese wedding?
journey.quote: For family practice, a clear record is the culture page of Girikerto village in Sleman, near Yogyakarta: a local account, not a rule for all of Java.
journey.reaction: Named source, and they tell me its limits. That's exactly how I'd want it framed.

journey.quote: The same 2022 study found that in the community it looked at, the tarub now stands only at the kitchen area, wedding tents take the front, and plastic flowers have replaced some decoration.
journey.reaction: Real-world detail from a study with a year on it, including the unglamorous bit. That reads like research, not a mood board.

journey.quote: It is often told that the bride's parents walk the couple forward wrapped in a sindur cloth (sindur binayang), and that the bride's father takes both on his lap in a step called timbang or pangkon.
journey.reaction: 'It is often told' shows up a lot, maybe ten times. I appreciate the honesty, but by the panggih section it starts to feel like a lot of the most recognisable customs have no source at all. I'd be cross-checking these.

journey.quote: We have not found an official source that sets out those differences.
journey.reaction: Rare for a wedding site to admit it couldn't find something. That buys more trust than a confident table would have.

journey.quote: Its listing does not single out weddings, but many couples choose live gamelan for the panggih and the reception.
journey.reaction: They didn't stretch the UNESCO listing to say more than it does. Fine. 'Many couples' has no number behind it, but it's a minor point.

journey.section: Can Australians legally marry in Java or Bali?
journey.quote: Civil Registry Offices do not normally accept a CNI issued more than 3 months before.
journey.reaction: An actual number I can plan around, alongside the 10-day notice. This is the most useful section for me.

journey.section: Can Australians legally marry in Java or Bali?
journey.quote: Under Indonesian Law No. 1 of 1974, both partners must hold the same religion, or one must convert.
journey.reaction: That's the catch, and they've put it up front with the law named. A sales page would bury that. Big trust gain.

journey.section: Can Australians legally marry in Java or Bali?
journey.quote: This reflects official guidance as at November 2026 and is not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated and limited. Good, though I'd like the date each source was checked rather than just the month.

journey.section: Planning a Javanese wedding with both families
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for everything around them, with the fee and inclusions agreed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'Fee and inclusions agreed in writing before you commit' is the right thing to say to me. Still no word on whether you take a cut from suppliers, but I don't expect a fee table in a culture article.

journey.section: Planning a Javanese wedding with both families
journey.quote: If you are weighing Java, Bali or a wedding at home, [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge) is a good place to begin that conversation.
journey.reaction: Soft, and it comes after all the evidence, which is the right order. It doesn't tell me if you actually have people on the ground in Yogyakarta or Solo, though.

unanswered_questions: Do you take commission or mark-ups from venues, juru paes or gamelan groups you recommend? (Business details are deferred, so I don't expect it in this article.)
Do you actually plan weddings in Java, or mainly Bali? Do you have vetted juru paes or elders you work with there?
Is there a real Javanese or Javanese-Australian wedding on your site with the actual budget I can look at?
Which date were the embassy and Smartraveller pages last checked, not just the month?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Javanese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Clickbait headline. Mild, because the body is the opposite of clickbait, but it nearly made me bounce from the search results.

would_share_with: My partner, if her family were Javanese, for the legal section on religion and the CNI timing

cta_reaction.quote: If you are weighing Java, Bali or a wedding at home, [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge) is a good place to begin that conversation.
cta_reaction.why: The article earned it, and the 'fee and inclusions agreed in writing' line helps. I'd look at the Concierge page, but I won't enquire until I see the fee model and a straight answer on supplier commissions. That belongs on the business page, not here.

top_3_changes: Tone down the headline: 'You Did Not Know?' oversells a page whose strength is careful sourcing.
Cut back on the 'It is often told' hedges, or name a source for at least one or two of the best-known panggih customs (egg-stepping, sindur, pangkon) so it doesn't come across as hand-waving.
In the closing section, say plainly whether Wedded Wonderland plans in Java itself (not just Bali), so I know whether the CTA applies to me.

checks.check: every point has an exact quote from the draft
no invented brand facts; fee, commission and Java coverage questions logged as unanswered
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots, CTA marker) treated as invisible
deferred business details and no-prices standard not raised as must-fix

open_questions.question: Daniel's main blockers to enquiring are fee model and supplier commissions. Both are deferred to business details, so they're not must-fix here. Should the Concierge landing page cover them?
Does Wedded Wonderland service Java (Yogyakarta, Solo) or only Bali? The closing section implies both. If Java isn't serviced, the CTA wording may need adjusting.

assumptions: Daniel's relevance is moderate: he'd only land here with a personal link (e.g. a partner's Javanese family). Without one, the topic is outside his brief.
FAST MODE: one skim pass in his reading order, FAQ first and then top to bottom.
